## Research questions

Our main question is how much the price-per-ping gap between high-rise and
walk-up apartment sales changes after accounting for district and floor area.
As a secondary question, we test whether adding those variables improves
predictions for transactions left out of model fitting.

The proposal also asks whether housing-price relationships vary across place,
time, and market segment. The current weekly data are heavily concentrated in
2026, and completion dates are unavailable for the 2026 analysis sample. We
therefore treat the current results as a focused analysis of the available
2026 sales. We test district-specific differences in the building-type gap
only where both building types have enough observations for a cautious
comparison. MRT accessibility remains a proposed extension, subject to
reliable address matching.

These are associations in recorded sales. The models do not identify causal
effects. District is used as a statistical adjustment variable here. We do
not label it a causal confounder without a causal design and assumptions.

## Team roles and handoffs

| Role | Main responsibility | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Data and sample | Check fields, units, exclusions, missing values, and district-by-type counts. | Freeze the shared analysis sample. |
| 2. Regression | Fit the three nested association models and check estimates and intervals. | Deliver the model table. |
| 3. Prediction and diagnostics | Compare out-of-sample errors and inspect residual and subgroup error patterns. | State what predicts well and where errors remain. |
| 4. Report and presentation | Render this report, prepare the main results slide, and coordinate the optional extension. | Deliver the checked report and presentation. |

## 1. Prepare the common analysis sample

The cleaning script creates the processed file. We retain eligible 2026
high-rise and walk-up sales with positive price per ping and floor area and a
recorded district. All three association models and the prediction comparison
use the same eligible observations.

```{r}
required_packages <- c("sandwich", "ggplot2")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Install required packages first: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}
library(ggplot2)

sales <- read.csv(
  "data/processed/taipei_residential_sales.csv",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

required_columns <- c(
  "year", "building_group", "price_per_ping_10k_ntd", "FAREA", "DISTRICT"
)
missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(sales))
if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop("Missing columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}

analysis_data <- subset(
  sales,
  year == 2026 &
    building_group %in% c("High-rise (11+ floors)", "Walk-up apartment") &
    is.finite(price_per_ping_10k_ntd) & price_per_ping_10k_ntd > 0 &
    is.finite(FAREA) & FAREA > 0 &
    !is.na(DISTRICT) & nzchar(DISTRICT)
)

analysis_data$building_group <- factor(
  analysis_data$building_group,
  levels = c("Walk-up apartment", "High-rise (11+ floors)")
)
analysis_data$DISTRICT <- factor(analysis_data$DISTRICT)
analysis_data$log_price_per_ping <- log(analysis_data$price_per_ping_10k_ntd)
analysis_data$log_area <- log(analysis_data$FAREA)

if (nrow(analysis_data) == 0) stop("No eligible 2026 transactions found.")

district_names <- c(
  "中正區" = "Zhongzheng", "大同區" = "Datong", "中山區" = "Zhongshan",
  "松山區" = "Songshan", "大安區" = "Da'an", "萬華區" = "Wanhua",
  "信義區" = "Xinyi", "士林區" = "Shilin", "北投區" = "Beitou",
  "內湖區" = "Neihu", "南港區" = "Nangang", "文山區" = "Wenshan"
)

district_counts <- as.data.frame.matrix(
  with(analysis_data, table(DISTRICT, building_group))
)
district_counts$District <- district_names[rownames(district_counts)]
district_counts <- district_counts[, c("District", setdiff(names(district_counts), "District"))]
rownames(district_counts) <- NULL

sample_summary <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Eligible transactions", "High-rise sales", "Walk-up sales"),
  Count = c(
    nrow(analysis_data),
    sum(analysis_data$building_group == "High-rise (11+ floors)"),
    sum(analysis_data$building_group == "Walk-up apartment")
  )
)
knitr::kable(sample_summary, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Analysis sample")
knitr::kable(district_counts, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Transactions by district and building type")
```

The supplied snapshot is expected to produce 247 eligible sales: 158
high-rises and 89 walk-ups. Check these counts before interpreting results.

## 2. Association analysis with three nested models

The outcome is log price per ping. Walk-up apartments are the reference group.
The building-type coefficient estimates the high-rise difference relative to
walk-ups. Model 2 adds district indicators. Model 3 also adds log floor area.

```{r}
model_1 <- lm(log_price_per_ping ~ building_group, data = analysis_data)
model_2 <- lm(log_price_per_ping ~ building_group + DISTRICT, data = analysis_data)
model_3 <- lm(
  log_price_per_ping ~ building_group + DISTRICT + log_area,
  data = analysis_data
)

models <- list(
  "1. Building type" = model_1,
  "2. Add district" = model_2,
  "3. Add floor area" = model_3
)

extract_gap <- function(model, model_name) {
  term <- "building_groupHigh-rise (11+ floors)"
  robust_vcov <- sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC3")
  estimate <- coef(model)[term]
  se <- sqrt(robust_vcov[term, term])
  critical <- qt(0.975, df = df.residual(model))

  data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    N = nobs(model),
    Gap_percent = 100 * (exp(estimate) - 1),
    CI_low = 100 * (exp(estimate - critical * se) - 1),
    CI_high = 100 * (exp(estimate + critical * se) - 1),
    R_squared = summary(model)$r.squared,
    In_sample_RMSE_log = sqrt(mean(residuals(model)^2)),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

gap_results <- do.call(rbind, Map(extract_gap, models, names(models)))
rownames(gap_results) <- NULL

gap_table <- transform(
  gap_results,
  Gap_percent = round(Gap_percent, 1),
  CI_low = round(CI_low, 1),
  CI_high = round(CI_high, 1),
  R_squared = round(R_squared, 3),
  In_sample_RMSE_log = round(In_sample_RMSE_log, 3)
)
knitr::kable(
  gap_table,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Model", "N", "Gap (%)", "95% CI low (%)", "95% CI high (%)",
                "In-sample R-squared", "In-sample RMSE, log price"),
  caption = "Adjusted high-rise price-per-ping gap relative to walk-ups"
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(gap_results, aes(x = Gap_percent, y = reorder(Model, Gap_percent))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey65", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = CI_low, xmax = CI_high),
    width = 0.16, orientation = "y", color = "#315B7D", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(color = "#C45A36", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated high-rise price gap across models",
    x = "Difference from walk-up apartments (%)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Points are estimates; bars are 95% HC3 confidence intervals."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

These three models are a **stepwise adjustment sequence**. They show how the
estimated association changes when district and floor area are added. They do
not, by themselves, show that prediction accuracy keeps improving. In-sample
R-squared cannot fall when predictors are added to nested ordinary least
squares models. We assess prediction separately below.

## 3. Prediction check on held-out transactions

The proposal asks whether property and location information improves
predictions for unseen transactions. We use repeated stratified five-fold
cross-validation. Each sale is predicted by models fitted without that fold.
The same folds are used for all three models. Errors are measured on the log
price-per-ping scale, so compare models within this analysis rather than
reading the error as NT dollars.

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
k_folds <- 5
n_repeats <- 20
strata <- interaction(analysis_data$DISTRICT, analysis_data$building_group, drop = TRUE)
cv_rows <- vector("list", n_repeats * k_folds * length(models))
row_number <- 1

for (repeat_id in seq_len(n_repeats)) {
  fold_id <- integer(nrow(analysis_data))

  for (stratum in levels(strata)) {
    rows <- which(strata == stratum)
    rows <- sample(rows)
    fold_id[rows] <- rep(seq_len(k_folds), length.out = length(rows))
  }

  for (fold in seq_len(k_folds)) {
    train_data <- analysis_data[fold_id != fold, , drop = FALSE]
    test_data <- analysis_data[fold_id == fold, , drop = FALSE]

    for (model_name in names(models)) {
      fitted_model <- lm(formula(models[[model_name]]), data = train_data)
      predicted <- predict(fitted_model, newdata = test_data)

      if (anyNA(predicted)) {
        stop("Cross-validation produced missing predictions. Check factor levels.")
      }

      cv_rows[[row_number]] <- data.frame(
        Repeat = repeat_id,
        Fold = fold,
        Model = model_name,
        Observed = test_data$log_price_per_ping,
        Predicted = as.numeric(predicted),
        Building_type = test_data$building_group,
        District = test_data$DISTRICT
      )
      row_number <- row_number + 1
    }
  }
}

cv_predictions <- do.call(rbind, cv_rows)
cv_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(cv_predictions, cv_predictions$Model), function(x) {
  data.frame(
    Model = x$Model[1],
    CV_RMSE_log = sqrt(mean((x$Observed - x$Predicted)^2)),
    CV_MAE_log = mean(abs(x$Observed - x$Predicted)),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}))
rownames(cv_summary) <- NULL
cv_summary$CV_RMSE_log <- round(cv_summary$CV_RMSE_log, 3)
cv_summary$CV_MAE_log <- round(cv_summary$CV_MAE_log, 3)
knitr::kable(cv_summary, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Model", "CV RMSE (log price)",
                           "CV MAE (log price)"),
             caption = "Repeated five-fold cross-validated prediction errors")
```

Lower cross-validated RMSE or MAE indicates better average prediction in this
sample and validation setup. The comparison tests whether adding district and
floor area improves prediction. It does not require LASSO or ridge because
these models contain a limited set of predictors. Those methods become more
relevant if the team expands to many predictors and wants to compare
regularized prediction models.

We also summarize cross-validated absolute error by building type. This helps
show whether one group is harder to predict.

```{r}
cv_by_type <- aggregate(
  abs(Observed - Predicted) ~ Model + Building_type,
  data = cv_predictions,
  FUN = mean
)
names(cv_by_type)[3] <- "Mean_absolute_error_log"
cv_by_type$Mean_absolute_error_log <- round(cv_by_type$Mean_absolute_error_log, 3)
knitr::kable(cv_by_type, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Model", "Building type",
                           "Mean absolute error (log price)"),
             caption = "Cross-validated absolute error by building type")
```

## 4. Extension: does the price gap differ by district?

The proposal asks whether price relationships vary across districts. We first
set a minimum coverage rule: include a district only when the analysis sample
contains at least eight sales of each building type there. The rule is based
on counts, before examining the estimated gaps. The current snapshot leaves
five districts that meet it.

Within those districts, we fit a model that allows the high-rise versus
walk-up gap to differ by district while accounting for log floor area. The
estimates are exploratory because the district-level groups remain small.

```{r}
district_table <- with(analysis_data, table(DISTRICT, building_group))
supported_districts <- rownames(district_table)[
  district_table[, "High-rise (11+ floors)"] >= 8 &
    district_table[, "Walk-up apartment"] >= 8
]

district_data <- droplevels(
  subset(analysis_data, DISTRICT %in% supported_districts)
)

district_gap_model <- lm(
  log_price_per_ping ~ building_group * DISTRICT + log_area,
  data = district_data
)

district_gap <- function(district, model, data) {
  new_data <- data.frame(
    building_group = factor(
      c("Walk-up apartment", "High-rise (11+ floors)"),
      levels = levels(data$building_group)
    ),
    DISTRICT = factor(district, levels = levels(data$DISTRICT)),
    log_area = mean(data$log_area)
  )

  design <- model.matrix(
    delete.response(terms(model)),
    new_data,
    contrasts.arg = model$contrasts
  )
  contrast <- design[2, ] - design[1, ]
  robust_vcov <- sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC3")
  estimate <- sum(contrast * coef(model))
  se <- sqrt(drop(contrast %*% robust_vcov %*% contrast))
  critical <- qt(0.975, df = df.residual(model))
  district_rows <- data[data$DISTRICT == district, , drop = FALSE]

  data.frame(
    District = unname(district_names[district]),
    High_rise_sales = sum(district_rows$building_group == "High-rise (11+ floors)"),
    Walk_up_sales = sum(district_rows$building_group == "Walk-up apartment"),
    Gap_percent = 100 * (exp(estimate) - 1),
    CI_low = 100 * (exp(estimate - critical * se) - 1),
    CI_high = 100 * (exp(estimate + critical * se) - 1),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

district_gap_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(supported_districts, district_gap,
         model = district_gap_model, data = district_data)
)
rownames(district_gap_results) <- NULL

district_gap_table <- transform(
  district_gap_results,
  Gap_percent = round(Gap_percent, 1),
  CI_low = round(CI_low, 1),
  CI_high = round(CI_high, 1)
)
knitr::kable(
  district_gap_table,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("District", "High-rise n", "Walk-up n", "Gap (%)",
                "95% CI low (%)", "95% CI high (%)"),
  caption = "District-specific adjusted price gaps in districts meeting the count rule"
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(district_gap_results, aes(x = Gap_percent, y = reorder(District, Gap_percent))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey65", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = CI_low, xmax = CI_high),
    width = 0.16, orientation = "y", color = "#315B7D", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(color = "#C45A36", size = 2.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted price gaps across supported districts",
    x = "High-rise difference from walk-ups (%)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "At least eight sales of each type per district; 95% HC3 intervals."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

This extension asks whether a single citywide gap describes the districts
with adequate sample overlap. Wide or overlapping intervals mean the data do
not precisely distinguish district-specific gaps. Do not rank districts or
claim a difference from point estimates alone.

## 5. Residual diagnostics

Residuals are the differences between observed and fitted log price per ping
for the same transactions used to fit Model 3. They are useful for checking
whether a pattern remains, but they are not the same as test-set prediction
errors. The cross-validation section above evaluates predictions on held-out
folds.

```{r}
diagnostic_data <- data.frame(
  Fitted = fitted(model_3),
  Residual = residuals(model_3),
  Floor_area = analysis_data$FAREA
)

ggplot(diagnostic_data, aes(x = Fitted, y = Residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, color = "#315B7D") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              color = "#C45A36", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Model 3 residuals by fitted value",
       x = "Fitted log price per ping", y = "Residual") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggplot(diagnostic_data, aes(x = Floor_area, y = Residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, color = "#315B7D") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              color = "#C45A36", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Model 3 residuals by floor area",
       x = "Floor area (ping)", y = "Residual in log price per ping") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

Look for a curve, changing spread, or clusters. A pattern can suggest that a
relevant feature is missing or that a relationship is not well represented.
Do not add variables solely to force residuals toward zero. Record the pattern,
propose a defensible adjustment, then compare it on the same sample and in
cross-validation.

## 6. Proposal extension: accessibility and location

The proposal names MRT accessibility and nearby amenities as optional
extensions. The current transaction file contains `LOCATION` addresses. If
the team wants one spatial extension, start with distance to the nearest MRT
entrance. Taipei publishes address-coordinate data and MRT entrance
coordinates. The work would be to match transaction addresses to coordinates,
calculate distance to the nearest entrance, report the address-match rate,
and add distance to Model 3. Define clearly whether the measure is straight
line distance or walking distance. Do not describe distance as travel time
unless a pedestrian route network is used.

This extension asks whether proximity adds information after district and
floor area are included. It is an association, and it should be kept only if
the geocoding match is reliable. Avoid adding MRT, bus stops, malls, tourist
sites, and an undefined “egg-yolk/egg-white” classification all at once.

## 7. Limits and next steps

- The current regression sample describes recorded 2026 sales in this snapshot.
- Earlier years are sparse in this weekly snapshot, so a 2019–2026 trend or
  time-varying price gap needs a better-covered historical extract.
- Completion dates are missing for the current sample, so building-age effects
  cannot be tested here.
- Elevator status overlaps with building type in this sample, so a separate
  elevator premium is not identified by this specification.
- The adjusted association models do not establish causality. Unmeasured
  factors such as exact micro-location, renovation, view, and building quality
  may remain.
- The district-by-building-type interaction is explored above only for
  districts meeting the stated minimum-count rule.

## Presentation sequence

1. State the research question and show the eligible sample.
2. Use the existing district and building-type plots to describe the data.
3. Show the three adjusted-gap estimates and explain that they trace the
   association as controls are added.
4. Show cross-validated errors separately to answer whether added predictors
   improve prediction on held-out transactions.
5. Show the district interaction as an exploratory check of whether the gap
   varies by location, with district counts and confidence intervals.
6. Use residual plots to discuss remaining patterns and limits.
7. Present nearest-MRT distance only if address matching is reliable; otherwise
   keep it as a proposed extension.
